value.rationale: Two-extension resilience is a natural adversarial robustness invariant controlling fixed-variable logical equivalence, not a chosen arithmetic slice. The result is complete for all prime powers and ambient dimensions in the rank-two Grassmann family, with a sharp uniform q+1 squared threshold, one exceptional graph with six-witness bottleneck, and a structural description of every minimum destructive deletion set. It quantifies the exact number of arbitrary vertex faults tolerated by a canonical dense distance-regular graph family, of potential relevance when constructing explicit FO^3-indistinguishable finite examples and fault-tolerant extension structures.
